items.title: Regulatory Affairs Managers
items.text: Review all regulatory agency submission materials to ensure timeliness, accuracy, comprehensiveness, or compliance with regulatory standards.

items.title: Purchasing Managers
items.text: Locate vendors of materials, equipment or supplies, and interview them to determine product availability and terms of sales.

items.title: Property, Real Estate, and Community Association Managers
items.text: Manage and oversee operations, maintenance, administration, and improvement of commercial, industrial, or residential properties.

items.title: Construction Managers
items.text: Plan, organize, or direct activities concerned with the construction or maintenance of structures, facilities, or systems.

items.title: Purchasing Managers
items.text: Prepare reports regarding market conditions and merchandise costs.

items.title: Compensation, Benefits, and Job Analysis Specialists
items.text: Plan and develop curricula and materials for training programs and conduct training.

items.title: Accountants and Auditors
items.text: Establish tables of accounts and assign entries to proper accounts.

items.title: Government Property Inspectors and Investigators
items.text: Examine records, reports, or other documents to establish facts or detect discrepancies.

items.title: Budget Analysts
items.text: Provide advice and technical assistance with cost analysis, fiscal allocation, and budget preparation.

items.title: Personal Financial Advisors
items.text: Manage client portfolios, keeping client plans up-to-date.

items.title: Web Developers
items.text: Evaluate or recommend server hardware or software.

items.title: Computer Systems Analysts
items.text: Review and analyze computer printouts and performance indicators to locate code problems, and correct errors by correcting codes.

items.title: Geographic Information Systems Technologists and Technicians
items.text: Create, analyze, report, convert, or transfer data, using specialized applications program software.

items.title: Computer Programmers
items.text: Perform or direct revision, repair, or expansion of existing programs to increase operating efficiency or adapt to new requirements.

items.title: Database Administrators
items.text: Test programs or databases, correct errors, and make necessary modifications.

items.title: Electronics Engineers, Except Computer
items.text: Analyze electronics system requirements, capacity, cost, or customer needs to determine project feasibility.

items.title: Energy Engineers, Except Wind and Solar
items.text: Analyze, interpret, or create graphical representations of energy data, using engineering software.

items.title: Robotics Engineers
items.text: Document robotic application development, maintenance, or changes.

items.title: Robotics Engineers
items.text: Design software to control robotic systems for applications, such as military defense or manufacturing.

items.title: Civil Engineering Technologists and Technicians
items.text: Prepare reports and document project activities and data.

items.title: Food Science Technicians
items.text: Compute moisture or salt content, percentages of ingredients, formulas, or other product factors, using mathematical and chemical procedures.

items.title: Urban and Regional Planners
items.text: Research, compile, analyze and organize information from maps, reports, investigations, and books for use in reports and special projects.

items.title: Biologists
items.text: Study aquatic plants and animals and environmental conditions affecting them, such as radioactivity or pollution.

items.title: Survey Researchers
items.text: Review, classify, and record survey data in preparation for computer analysis.

items.title: Industrial Ecologists
items.text: Examine societal issues and their relationship with both technical systems and the environment.

items.title: Health Education Specialists
items.text: Prepare and distribute health education materials, such as reports, bulletins, and visual aids, to address smoking, vaccines, and other public health concerns.

items.title: Educational, Guidance, and Career Counselors and Advisors
items.text: Teach classes and present self-help or information sessions on subjects related to education and career planning.

items.title: Educational, Guidance, and Career Counselors and Advisors
items.text: Plan, direct, and participate in recruitment and enrollment activities.

items.title: Mental Health and Substance Abuse Social Workers
items.text: Monitor, evaluate, and record client progress with respect to treatment goals.

items.title: Substance Abuse and Behavioral Disorder Counselors
items.text: Provide clients or family members with information about addiction issues and about available services or programs, making appropriate referrals when necessary.

items.title: Judges, Magistrate Judges, and Magistrates
items.text: Research legal issues and write opinions on the issues.

items.title: Arbitrators, Mediators, and Conciliators
items.text: Apply relevant laws, regulations, policies, or precedents to reach conclusions.

items.title: Arbitrators, Mediators, and Conciliators
items.text: Use mediation techniques to facilitate communication between disputants, to further parties' understanding of different perspectives, and to guide parties toward mutual agreement.

items.title: Paralegals and Legal Assistants
items.text: Gather and analyze research data, such as statutes, decisions, and legal articles, codes, and documents.

items.title: Judges, Magistrate Judges, and Magistrates
items.text: Write decisions on cases.

items.title: Teaching Assistants, Postsecondary
items.text: Prepare or proctor examinations.

items.title: Elementary School Teachers, Except Special Education
items.text: Organize and label materials and display students' work.

items.title: Library Science Teachers, Postsecondary
items.text: Keep abreast of developments in the field by reading current literature, talking with colleagues, giving presentations at conferences, and serving on committees in professional associations.

items.title: Business Teachers, Postsecondary
items.text: Advise students on academic and vocational curricula and career issues.

items.title: Chemistry Teachers, Postsecondary
items.text: Prepare and deliver lectures to undergraduate or graduate students on topics such as organic chemistry, analytical chemistry, and chemical separation.

items.title: Special Effects Artists and Animators
items.text: Use models to simulate the behavior of animated objects in the finished sequence.

items.title: Craft Artists
items.text: Develop concepts or creative ideas for craft objects.

items.title: Technical Writers
items.text: Review published materials and recommend revisions or changes in scope, format, content, and methods of reproduction and binding.

items.title: News Analysts, Reporters, and Journalists
items.text: Check reference materials, such as books, news files, or public records, to obtain relevant facts.

items.title: Art Directors
items.text: Create custom illustrations or other graphic elements.

items.title: Nurse Midwives
items.text: Read current literature, talk with colleagues, or participate in professional organizations or conferences to keep abreast of developments in midwifery.

items.title: Family Medicine Physicians
items.text: Collect, record, and maintain patient information, such as medical history, reports, or examination results.

items.title: Dermatologists
items.text: Record patients' health histories.

items.title: Advanced Practice Psychiatric Nurses
items.text: Educate patients and family members about mental health and medical conditions, preventive health measures, medications, or treatment plans.

items.title: Acupuncturists
items.text: Collect medical histories and general health and lifestyle information from patients.

items.title: Medical Assistants
items.text: Schedule appointments for patients.

items.title: Endoscopy Technicians
items.text: Read current literature, talk with colleagues, or participate in professional organizations or conferences to keep abreast of developments in endoscopy.

items.title: Medical Transcriptionists
items.text: Perform data entry and data retrieval services, providing data for inclusion in medical records and for transmission to physicians.

items.title: Medical Transcriptionists
items.text: Transcribe dictation for a variety of medical reports, such as patient histories, physical examinations, emergency room visits, operations, chart reviews, consultation, or discharge summaries.

items.title: Physical Therapist Aides
items.text: Schedule patient appointments with physical therapists and coordinate therapists' schedules.

items.title: Customs and Border Protection Officers
items.text: Examine immigration applications, visas, and passports and interview persons to determine eligibility for admission, residence, and travel in the U.S.

items.title: Retail Loss Prevention Specialists
items.text: Prepare written reports on investigations.

items.title: Intelligence Analysts
items.text: Design, use, or maintain databases and software applications, such as geographic information systems (GIS) mapping and artificial intelligence tools.

items.title: Police and Sheriff's Patrol Officers
items.text: Record facts to prepare reports that document incidents and activities.

items.title: Transit and Railroad Police
items.text: Prepare reports documenting investigation activities and results.

items.title: Concierges
items.text: Plan special events, parties, or meetings, which may include booking musicians or celebrities.

items.title: Childcare Workers
items.text: Create developmentally appropriate lesson plans.

items.title: Baggage Porters and Bellhops
items.text: Supply guests or travelers with directions, travel information, and other information, such as available services and points of interest.

items.title: Hairdressers, Hairstylists, and Cosmetologists
items.text: Schedule client appointments.

items.title: Amusement and Recreation Attendants
items.text: Provide information about facilities, entertainment options, and rules and regulations.

items.title: Real Estate Sales Agents
items.text: Answer clients' questions regarding construction work, financing, maintenance, repairs, and appraisals.

items.title: Securities, Commodities, and Financial Services Sales Agents
items.text: Buy or sell stocks, bonds, commodity futures, foreign currencies, or other securities on behalf of investment dealers.

items.title: Sales Representatives, Wholesale and Manufacturing, Technical and Scientific Products
items.text: Contact new or existing customers to discuss how specific products or services can meet their needs.

items.title: Sales Representatives, Wholesale and Manufacturing, Technical and Scientific Products
items.text: Select or assist customers in selecting products based on customer needs, product specifications, and applicable regulations.

items.title: Sales Representatives, Wholesale and Manufacturing, Except Technical and Scientific Products
items.text: Identify prospective customers by using business directories, following leads from existing clients, participating in organizations and clubs, and attending trade shows and conferences.

items.title: Executive Secretaries and Executive Administrative Assistants
items.text: Review operating practices and procedures to determine whether improvements can be made in areas such as workflow, reporting procedures, or expenditures.

items.title: Legal Secretaries and Administrative Assistants
items.text: Schedule and make appointments.

items.title: Secretaries and Administrative Assistants, Except Legal, Medical, and Executive
items.text: Develop or maintain internal or external company Web sites.

items.title: Credit Authorizers, Checkers, and Clerks
items.text: Prepare reports of findings and recommendations.

items.title: Order Clerks
items.text: Inform customers by mail or telephone of order information, such as unit prices, shipping dates, and any anticipated delays.

items.title: Construction and Building Inspectors
items.text: Review and interpret plans, blueprints, site layouts, specifications, or construction methods to ensure compliance to legal requirements and safety regulations.

items.title: Plumbers, Pipefitters, and Steamfitters
items.text: Review blueprints, building codes, or specifications to determine work details or procedures.

items.title: First-Line Supervisors of Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers
items.text: Develop or implement electronic maintenance programs or computer information management systems.

items.title: Computer, Automated Teller, and Office Machine Repairers
items.text: Install and configure new equipment, including operating software or peripheral equipment.

items.title: Security and Fire Alarm Systems Installers
items.text: Prepare documents, such as invoices or warranties.

items.title: Computer, Automated Teller, and Office Machine Repairers
items.text: Analyze equipment performance records to assess equipment functioning.

items.title: Camera and Photographic Equipment Repairers
items.text: Record test data and document fabrication techniques on reports.

items.title: Timing Device Assemblers and Adjusters
items.text: Review blueprints, sketches, or work orders to gather information about tasks to be completed.

items.title: Computer Numerically Controlled Tool Programmers
items.text: Modify existing programs to enhance efficiency.

items.title: Inspectors, Testers, Sorters, Samplers, and Weighers
items.text: Analyze test data, making computations as necessary, to determine test results.

items.title: Mixing and Blending Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
items.text: Record operational or production data on specified forms.

items.title: Electrical and Electronic Equipment Assemblers
items.text: Read and interpret schematic drawings, diagrams, blueprints, specifications, work orders, or reports to determine materials requirements or assembly instructions.

items.title: Flight Attendants
items.text: Answer passengers' questions about flights, aircraft, weather, travel routes and services, arrival times, or schedules.

items.title: First-Line Supervisors of Helpers, Laborers, and Material Movers, Hand
items.text: Participate in the hiring process by reviewing credentials, conducting interviews, or making hiring decisions or recommendations.
